en.title: Sum of Distinct Integer-Division Quotients
en.description:
Given a positive integer n, consider floor(n/k) for every positive integer k. Sum the distinct quotient values that occur. k may exceed n, in which case the quotient is 0, which does not affect the sum. Each quotient value is counted only once.

The standard input format, examples, and test data were written by CSWork.
en.input: Input n (1..10¹⁰); use a 64-bit integer to store the result.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: When n=5, the distinct quotients are 5, 2, 1, 0, and their sum is 8.
hints: Start from k=1. The current quotient q=n//k stays the same over the whole range [k,n//q]; add q once and jump directly to n//q+1.
